cases.question: How should I keep offline information available during a power or internet outage? Use the kit sources. At most 100 words.
cases.answer: To keep offline information available during a power or internet outage, prioritize printing essential guides like the survival priorities and first aid medicine. Use the 72-hour kit checklist to prepare before a crisis, ensuring you have a list of food, medicines, and tools. Store these guides in a waterproof, fireproof container. Practice using these skills before a crisis to ensure you can act quickly and safely. [2], [3], [4]

sources.section: Order of consumption in a crisis
sources.text:
1. Food from the fridge (after 2–4 hours without power it starts warming up; keep the door closed).
2. Freezer (full and closed it holds for about 48 hours; half full, about 24 hours).
3. Fresh fruit and vegetables.
4. Dry stock and canned goods.

> Source: USDA — Food Safety During Power Outage. https://www.foodsafety.gov/food-safety-charts/food-safety-during-power-outage

- Browse the **index** in the web interface or ask the local AI.
- Print the most critical guides (water, first aid, fire) — paper doesn't need power.
- Practice **before** the crisis: making fire, purifying water, CPR and tourniquets are learned with your hands.

1. **Immediate safety:** leave hazardous areas (fire, flood, collapse, gas). Shut off the gas and the main power switch if there is a leak or water in the wiring.
2. **Injured people:** control severe bleeding, check breathing (see [First aid](07-first-aid-medicine.md)).
3. **Communication:** agree with your family on a meeting point and a fixed time to try to make contact by radio/phone.
4. **Body temperature:** dry clothes, shelter, insulation from the ground.
5. **Water:** store all the clean water you can (tanks, bathtubs, bottles) before the mains pressure runs out. Plan on at least 3 liters per person per day just for drinking.
6. **Inventory:** list food, medicines, fuel, batteries, tools and who needs special care (babies, elderly people, the chronically ill, pets).
7. **Information:** a battery- or crank-powered AM/FM radio is the most reliable official source when the internet goes down.
Use these lists to prepare **before** and to take inventory **during** a crisis. Adjust to your family size, climate and special needs.

This guide is the starting point. When the internet, power and public services stop, the order in which you act matters more than any piece of equipment.

> ⚠️ **Warning:** this material is educational and does not replace health professionals, firefighters or civil defense. Whenever help is available, seek it (in Brazil: SAMU ambulance 192, Fire Department 193, Civil Defense 199; elsewhere: 911 in the US/Canada, 112 in Europe).

sources.doc_title: Checklists: kit de 72 horas e estoque para 1 ano
sources.section: Casa: estoque para 1 ano (por adulto, aproximado)
sources.text:
### Água
- [ ] Reservatório de 50–100 L por pessoa + sistema de captação de chuva
- [ ] Filtro de cerâmica/membrana com velas/elementos de reposição
- [ ] Água sanitária sem perfume (renovar a cada 6 meses) ou hipoclorito de cálcio granulado (dura mais)

### Comida
- [ ] 150–180 kg de grãos (arroz, trigo, milho, aveia, farinhas)
- [ ] 30–40 kg de leguminosas
- [ ] 10–12 L de óleo/gordura
- [ ] 25–30 kg de açúcar/mel
- [ ] 3–5 kg de sal (mais para conservas)
- [ ] Leite em pó, fermento, bicarbonato, vinagre, temperos
- [ ] Multivitamínico (365 doses)
- [ ] Moedor de grãos manual
- [ ] Sementes crioulas de hortaliças, feijão, milho, abóbora

### Saúde
- [ ] Kit de primeiros socorros completo (veja [Primeiros socorros](07-first-aid-medicine.md))
- [ ] Remédios de uso contínuo para o máximo de meses que a receita permitir
- [ ] Sais de reidratação oral (vários envelopes)
- [ ] Óculos reserva, aparelhos auditivos e pilhas
- [ ] Livros impressos: *Onde Não Há Médico*, *Onde Não Há Dentista*

### Fogo, energia e luz
- [ ] Isqueiros (10+), fósforos (vários maços), 2 pederneiras
- [ ] Lenha seca e/ou carvão; fogareiro e combustível
- [ ] Painel solar + controlador + bateria
- [ ] Lanternas LED, pilhas recarregáveis + carregador solar
- [ ] Velas e óleo para lamparinas

### Higiene
- [ ] Sabão em barra e em pó, detergente
- [ ] Papel higiênico, sacos de lixo resistentes, cal virgem/hidratada
- [ ] Baldes com tampa (latrina de emergência)
- [ ] Repelente, protetor solar, mosquiteiros

### Ferramentas e materiais
- [ ] Veja [Ferramentas](12-tools-knots-repairs.md): faca, machado, serrote, pá, enxada, martelo, pregos, cordas, lona, fita silver tape, arame
- [ ] Kit de costura
- [ ] Kit de reparo de bicicleta

### Comunicação e informação
- [ ] Rádio AM/FM/ondas curtas
- [ ] Rádios comunicadores (PX, PMR/FRS ou radioamador)
- [ ] Notebook ou mini PC com este kit e as bases Kiwix; cópia em HD externo
- [ ] Guias impressos dos capítulos críticos deste repositório

Este guia é o ponto de partida. Quando a internet, a energia e os serviços param, a ordem das ações importa mais do que qualquer equipamento.

> ⚠️ **Aviso:** este material é educativo e não substitui profissionais de saúde, bombeiros ou defesa civil. Sempre que houver socorro disponível, procure-o (no Brasil: SAMU 192, Bombeiros 193, Defesa Civil 199).
Em crises circulam boatos. Confie em fontes oficiais (Defesa Civil, rádios locais) e confirme informações com mais de uma fonte antes de agir.
Escreva em papel tudo que for aprendendo (receitas, mapas, contatos, consertos). Bibliotecas offline como o iFixit (disponível no Kiwix) ensinam a consertar milhares de aparelhos.

sources.text:
- Mantenha este kit (Emergency AI + bases Kiwix) em **pendrive e HD externo**, e uma cópia num notebook de baixo consumo.
- Um notebook rodando a IA local gasta ~30–60 W enquanto responde; um computador pequeno (mini PC, Raspberry Pi 5) gasta ~5–15 W.

> Fontes: CDC — Generator safety and carbon monoxide (https://www.cdc.gov/carbon-monoxide/); CRESESB/CEPEL — Manual de Engenharia para Sistemas Fotovoltaicos (2014); Liter of Light (litrodeluz).

cases.question: ¿Cómo mantener disponible la información sin conexión durante un corte de electricidad o internet? Usa las fuentes del kit. Máximo 100 palabras.
cases.answer: Para mantener disponible la información sin conexión durante un corte de electricidad o internet, puedes usar una radio AM/FM a pilas o a dinamo. Esta es la fuente oficial más confiable cuando se cae internet. Además, copia las bases Kiwix en un disco duro externo y usa un radio transmisor para recibir información.

sources.text:
1. **Seguridad inmediata:** salga de las zonas de riesgo (incendio, inundación, derrumbe, gas). Cierre el gas y corte la electricidad general si hay una fuga o agua en la instalación.
2. **Heridos:** controle los sangrados graves y verifique la respiración (vea [Primeros auxilios](07-first-aid-medicine.md)).
3. **Comunicación:** acuerde con la familia un punto de encuentro y un horario fijo para intentar contacto por radio/teléfono.
4. **Temperatura corporal:** ropa seca, refugio, aislamiento del suelo.
5. **Agua:** almacene toda el agua limpia posible (tanques, bañeras, botellas) antes de que se acabe la presión de la red. Calcule como mínimo 3 litros por persona por día solo para beber.

sources.doc_title: Energía, luz y electricidad sin la red
sources.section: Sistema solar simple (lo más útil a largo plazo)
sources.text:
Componentes:
1. **Panel solar** (ej.: 100–200 W, 12 V o 18 V nominal).
2. **Controlador de carga** (PWM o MPPT) — obligatorio, protege la batería.
3. **Batería** (12 V): de litio LiFePO4 (dura más, 2.000+ ciclos) o de plomo-ácido estacionaria/automotriz (más barata, no la descargue por debajo del 50%).
4. **Inversor** (12 V → 127/220 V) solo si necesita aparatos de enchufe; para USB y LED de 12 V, use la corriente directamente.

**Cuenta rápida:** energía (Wh) = potencia (W) × horas.
- Un panel de 100 W genera, en promedio, **300–500 Wh por día** en Brasil (3–5 horas de sol pleno equivalente; valores similares en la mayor parte de América Latina tropical).
- Celular: ~15 Wh por carga. Bombilla LED de 9 W durante 5 h: 45 Wh. Radio: 5 Wh. Laptop: 50–80 Wh por carga.
- Refrigerador pequeño eficiente: ~600–1.000 Wh/día (necesita 2–3 paneles y una batería grande).

Conexiones: panel → controlador → batería → cargas. Use un fusible cerca de la batería y el calibre de cable adecuado (12 V exige cables gruesos para que no se calienten).

Esta guía es el punto de partida. Cuando internet, la electricidad y los servicios se detienen, el orden de las acciones importa más que cualquier equipo.

> ⚠️ **Aviso:** este material es educativo y no sustituye a profesionales de la salud, bomberos ni protección civil. Siempre que haya ayuda disponible, búsquela (en Brasil: SAMU 192, Bomberos 193, Defensa Civil 199; 112 en la Unión Europea, 911 en gran parte de América).

sources.doc_title: Energía, luz y electricidad sin la red
sources.text:
- **Bicicleta con dinamo/generador:** carga baterías pequeñas (esfuerzo considerable para poca energía).
- **Microgenerador hidráulico** en un arroyo con desnivel: genera energía 24 h — excelente si existe la fuente.
- **Leña:** la energía más simple para cocinar y calentar. Manéjela: corte ramas en vez de árboles enteros, plante árboles de crecimiento rápido, seque la leña durante meses (la leña verde rinde la mitad y hace mucho humo).
- **Cocina solar** para cocinar sin leña (vea [Comida](04-food.md)).

sources.text:

sources.text:
- **Bicicleta con dinamo/generador:** carga baterías pequeñas (esfuerzo considerable para poca energía).

cases.question: How should I keep offline information available during a power or internet outage? Use the kit sources. At most 100 words.
cases.answer:
1. **Print critical guides** (water, first aid, fire) now; paper does not need power [2].
2. **Use a battery- or crank-powered AM/FM radio** as the most reliable source for official information when the internet goes down [3].
3. **Ask your local AI** to browse the kit's web interface for offline access [2].
4. **Agree on a meeting point** with your family to share information if communication fails [3].
*Note: This guide is educational and does not replace professional health or emergency services [5].*

sources.section: Order of consumption in a crisis
sources.text:
1. Food from the fridge (after 2–4 hours without power it starts warming up; keep the door closed).
2. Freezer (full and closed it holds for about 48 hours; half full, about 24 hours).
3. Fresh fruit and vegetables.
4. Dry stock and canned goods.

> Source: USDA — Food Safety During Power Outage. https://www.foodsafety.gov/food-safety-charts/food-safety-during-power-outage

- Browse the **index** in the web interface or ask the local AI.
- Print the most critical guides (water, first aid, fire) — paper doesn't need power.
- Practice **before** the crisis: making fire, purifying water, CPR and tourniquets are learned with your hands.

1. **Immediate safety:** leave hazardous areas (fire, flood, collapse, gas). Shut off the gas and the main power switch if there is a leak or water in the wiring.
2. **Injured people:** control severe bleeding, check breathing (see [First aid](07-first-aid-medicine.md)).
3. **Communication:** agree with your family on a meeting point and a fixed time to try to make contact by radio/phone.
4. **Body temperature:** dry clothes, shelter, insulation from the ground.
5. **Water:** store all the clean water you can (tanks, bathtubs, bottles) before the mains pressure runs out. Plan on at least 3 liters per person per day just for drinking.
6. **Inventory:** list food, medicines, fuel, batteries, tools and who needs special care (babies, elderly people, the chronically ill, pets).
7. **Information:** a battery- or crank-powered AM/FM radio is the most reliable official source when the internet goes down.
Use these lists to prepare **before** and to take inventory **during** a crisis. Adjust to your family size, climate and special needs.

This guide is the starting point. When the internet, power and public services stop, the order in which you act matters more than any piece of equipment.

> ⚠️ **Warning:** this material is educational and does not replace health professionals, firefighters or civil defense. Whenever help is available, seek it (in Brazil: SAMU ambulance 192, Fire Department 193, Civil Defense 199; elsewhere: 911 in the US/Canada, 112 in Europe).

sources.doc_title: Energía, luz y electricidad sin la red
sources.text:
- **Bicicleta con dinamo/generador:** carga baterías pequeñas (esfuerzo considerable para poca energía).
- **Microgenerador hidráulico** en un arroyo con desnivel: genera energía 24 h — excelente si existe la fuente.
- **Leña:** la energía más simple para cocinar y calentar. Manéjela: corte ramas en vez de árboles enteros, plante árboles de crecimiento rápido, seque la leña durante meses (la leña verde rinde la mitad y hace mucho humo).
- **Cocina solar** para cocinar sin leña (vea [Comida](04-food.md)).

cases.question: How should I keep offline information available during a power or internet outage? Use the kit sources. At most 100 words.
cases.answer: Store your offline data on a USB flash drive, external hard drive, and a low-power laptop [1]. Protect electronics from moisture using silica gel or airtight bags, and guard against power surges [1]. If using a laptop, expect 30–60 W consumption; mini PCs or Raspberry Pi 5 use only 5–15 W [1]. For power generation, ensure generators are outdoors to prevent carbon monoxide poisoning; never run them in enclosed spaces [1]. If you lack these specific sources, prioritize keeping devices dry and away from water or fuel sources.
